best_hook.why: Over tea, a nobleman casually waits for his cousin's death to be sealed so he can take the title - a villain plot stated outright.

best_cliffhanger.why: 'Not through the winter. I've ensured her quiet comfort' - he all but admits he is poisoning the old Duchess, and nobody stops him.

must_promos.why: Tight villain cut: claim the title once the cousin is declared dead, 'the old woman still breathes', and it ends on his veiled confession that he is killing her.
Fallen noblewoman in a barn vows 'I am not finished', then the schemers say she has 'no rival' and claim the house - dramatic irony that sets up a showdown.

standalone_risk: The poisoning is only implied, and a stranger cannot tell who Alexander, the Dowager or the barn woman are to the scheming couple; the barn and drawing-room scenes are never connected on screen.
notes: Mostly villain exposition with no confrontation; the strength comes from the implied murder plot.
